annotations.title: Til they ſee.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> To the Apoſtles, that had to preach the kingdom of God and to ſuffer ſo much miſerie for the ſame in this world, he wil ſhew his glorie, and giue them a taſt of his owne ioyful ſtate and of his Saincts in heauen, calling thither Moyſes and Elias, that the Law and Prophets might be witneſſes of the ſame. See the annotation vpon S. Matthew c. 17, 2.

annotations.title: Face to goe to Hieruſalem.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> <mn>[2]</mn> The Samaritans were Schiſmatikes from the Iewes, and had a Schiſmatical temple in mount Garizim, of purpoſe to draw men thither from Gods temple in Hieruſalem, where only was the true and as it were the Catholike ſeruice and Sacrifice vnto God. Therfore they did not gladly receiue our Sauiour, becauſe they perceiued he was going to Hieruſalem.

annotations.title: He rebuked them.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Not iuſtice nor all rigorous puniſhment of ſinners is here forbidden, nor Elias' fact reprehended, nor the Church or Chriſtian Princes blamed for putting Heretics to death: but that none of theſe ſhould be done for deſire of our particular reuenge, or without diſcretion, & regard of their amendment, and example to others. <mn>[2]</mn> Therefore S. Peter <mn>[3]</mn> vſed his power vpon Ananias and Sapphira, when he ſtrook them both downe to death for defrauding the Church.

annotations.title: No man looking backe.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> It is a dangerous temptation for a man that hath loſt or left his goods for Chriſt, to looke much backe at them, and to remember with delight the pleaſures and eaſes of this world. for it breedeth in him diſcontentment of the troubles and croſſes that are incident to the ſtate of ſuch as fully folow Chriſt. In which caſe a man ſhould euer looke forward towards heauen, and neuer backeward to the world.
